Mod Menu 1.5.6 fixes an interaction between spectator switching and effects supplied by enchanted armor.

- Leaving spectator for survival or creative clears only night vision, preserving other active potion effects. Previously the cleanup cleared every effect.
- All menu game-mode changes use a shared path that skips redundant writes and checks that a requested change succeeded. A blocked spectator change cannot continue its dependent teleport or be logged as successful.
- Read-only diagnostics record equipped/held enchantments before and after menu mode changes, plus nearby lead spawn timing and reported ownership. Follow-up samples run at 5, 10 and 20 ticks, with post-switch observation bounded to two seconds of wall-clock time.
- Item drops and enchantments are preserved. Diagnostic callbacks are invalidated on shutdown, replacement or a different login session.

Validation: 37 automated regressions cover selective effect cleanup, native Endstone 0.11.15 event/NBT contracts, item preservation, menu callbacks and diagnostic lifecycle. These are automated API/model checks; the reported live lead-drop cause has not been confirmed. Nearby spawn observations do not prove an enchantment caused the item.

Target: Endstone 0.11.15 / API 0.11 and BDS 1.26.60.6. The wheel is pure Python and requires Python 3.10+; the release workflow uses Python 3.11.

Install: stop the server, replace the previous Mod Menu wheel in plugins/ with endstone_mod_menu-1.5.6-py3-none-any.whl, keep existing plugin data, and restart. Keep one Mod Menu wheel installed. If the lead drop continues, compare with no armor and one enchanted piece at a time, then inspect [ModeSwitchDiagnostics] in the server log.
